issue_context.title: Provide way to fully clean up a release via CLI
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

When scripting release builds, the flow might go something like this:

- Create a draft release
- In parallel, build assets for the release (maybe, different flavors of an Android app), and add them to the release
- Finalize and mark the release no longer a draft if everything is good.

The issue comes if one of those parallel builds fails. If so, the release is incomplete, and it would be best if we could fully remove the release, its tag, and its assets. 

This relates to #378 

### Proposed solution

According to the linked ticket, and the docs, you cannot today remove the assets from a release. 

I propose implementing the original --assetID part of the release delete command request in #378. 

Then a user would run `gh release delete --user <user> --repo <repo> --tag <tag>` to fully delete everything about the release on github. You could use --tag if that's what you know, and if so, it would remove the tag and the related assets. 

If, instead, you only want to remove a specific asset, you could use  `gh release delete --user <user> --repo <repo> --assetID <assetID>` to remove only that asset from a release.
comments:
Thanks for the feature request!

> You could use --tag if that's what you know, and if so, it would remove the tag and the related assets.

I dig the idea of a separate flag that triggers the removing of the associated git tag as well 👍 

> `gh release delete ... --assetID <assetID>`

1. How would a person obtain the asset ID in the first place? I don't think we show IDs anywhere in `gh release view`.
2. But if the person wanted to delete only 1 asset, but omitted the `--assetID` flag by accident, they would end up accidentally deleting the entire release with all its assets, right? I'm wary of a command that means one thing with a flag but a more destructive thing without that flag. Maybe it would be best to have a separate `delete-asset` command 🤔

> * How would a person obtain the asset ID in the first place? I don't think we show IDs anywhere in `gh release view`.
> 
> * But if the person wanted to delete only 1 asset, but omitted the `--assetID` flag by accident, they would end up accidentally deleting the entire release with all its assets, right? I'm wary of a command that means one thing with a flag but a more destructive thing without that flag. Maybe it would be best to have a separate `delete-asset` command 🤔

As to how I would get the assetId, it seems reasonable that this could be returned when uploading an asset. I apologize for not checking ahead of time to see if that was returned. 

I was thinking about the same thing for the second point. I agree! I almost proposed `--force` but really, `--purge` or something like that might work well to trigger a full removal of all a release's metadata.

> it seems reasonable that this could be returned when uploading an asset.

So if you weren't the one who uploaded the asset in the first place, or if you did but your terminal history no longer contains the output of the original `gh release upload` command, then you wouldn't have access to the numeric ID?

How about deleting assets by name instead of ID? Names are unique and exposed in `gh release view`.

Names would work well. That's a good observation - for my various use cases building a release is not something that more than one person works on, but having all the data available via `gh release view` would be ideal. 

I didn't realize names were unique. Since they are...

`gh release delete ... --assetName <assetName>`

..would work just fine.

@mislav @inktomi This sounds like a good idea, may I pick this up ?
We need to add a new flag to the `release delete` command that will take the asset name and delete it from the draft release.

I'd be more than happy if you wanted to pick it up!
